name: MAS Boston Society
mission: Tarbiya Department Tarbiya aims at rooting the faith, purifying the soul, expanding and refining knowledge/understanding, developing and refining all aspects of character, boosting commitment, building skills, and instilling the discipline necessary to conduct a successful, fulfilling, meaningful, and balanced life of learning, virtue, commitment, and service of Islam and humanity.
theoryOfChange: MAS Boston Society has a published 'Our Impact Areas' page on their website. This page outlines four key focus areas: Islam for Muslims, Leadership Development, Community Mobilization, and Social Justice. For each focus area, the document details subareas of focus (activities) and expected outcomes, such as 'Knowledge,' 'Behavior,' 'Capacity,' 'Influence,' 'Network,' 'Scale,' 'Partnership,' and 'Strategic Alignment.' This structured approach describes how their programs and activities are intended to lead to specific impacts, functioning as an impact framework and program strategy document.

strengths_deep_dive: MAS Boston demonstrates strong historical financial directness, directing <cite id="6">80.7% of expenditures toward direct programs</cite> such as youth development, PACE, and convert support [5], [6]. This beats the 75% program-ratio benchmark [6]. Additionally, <cite id="6">fundraising efficiency was strong at 7%</cite>, leaving <cite id="6">$2,406,615 in direct public contributions</cite> well-utilized [6].
rich_narrative.summary: MAS Boston Society focuses on faith-based community development, youth programs, and civic engagement in the greater Boston area [5]. The organization maintains <cite id="1">verified zakat eligibility</cite> for specific religious categories, serving poor and needy populations [1]. However, <cite id="6">no financial filings newer than FY2018 are available</cite> — donors should treat this 8-year-old financial picture with caution, as it raises significant accountability questions [6]. In its FY2018 filing, MAS Boston reported <cite id="6">$3,286,832 in total revenue</cite> with a <cite id="6">high program expense ratio of 86.0%</cite> [6]. Fundraising operations remained efficient at <cite id="6">$0.07 per $1 raised</cite> [6]. Balanced against these historical operational strengths, the complete lack of recent financial disclosures and absence of verified outcome metrics limit donor visibility [6].
